headline: High risk of cascading errors and capability conflict; prompt-injection and leakage are limited by lack of shared channels.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Argo Workflows has no documented direct ingestion of xonsh output, and xonsh shows no clipboard or MCP bridge. The only plausible pathway is manual handoff or shared files, which is not documented here. That makes injection possible but not default, and the blast radius is limited by the lack of an explicit shared channel.
conditions: IF the operator copies xonsh output into an Argo parameter or manifest, prompt content can be interpreted as instructions.
IF a shared filesystem is introduced between the two agents, file-based injection becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Avoid copy-pasting model output into workflow specs.
Use a strict template for any handoff text.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Argo Workflows touches artifacts and parameters, while xonsh reads and writes the filesystem and environment variables. No shared workspace or authenticated principal is documented, so leakage is not established. The main risk is accidental exposure if operators move files between them, which is narrower than a default shared-data path.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory, xonsh can read artifacts produced by Argo.
IF sensitive parameters are written to files that xonsh can access, they may be exposed.
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent.
Store secrets outside shared artifacts.
Restrict file permissions on workflow outputs.
Review any file handoff before execution.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Argo Workflows can call REST/gRPC APIs and xonsh can execute shell commands, spawn subprocesses, and write the filesystem. Even without modify_git_state, both can mutate shared resources if orchestrated together. The overlap is enough for default coordination bugs or write races when they target the same files or APIs.
conditions: IF both agents target the same filesystem path, writes can race or overwrite each other.
IF Argo and xonsh share a mutable API resource, conflicting updates can occur without locking.
mitigations: Assign disjoint output paths.
Serialize writes through one orchestrator.
Use per-run unique filenames.
Check for existing locks before mutation.
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency controls.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Argo Workflows can pass artifacts and parameters downstream, and xonsh can execute shell commands based on those inputs. If Argo-produced content is treated as authoritative by xonsh, an error can cascade into real actions or corrupted outputs. The pair lacks a documented verification boundary, so uncertainty pushes this to high.
conditions: IF xonsh consumes Argo-generated parameters without validation, bad upstream data can trigger downstream commands.
IF Argo artifacts are used as shell input, a single bad artifact can propagate into multiple steps.
mitigations: Validate all upstream parameters before shell use.
Require human review for action-bearing outputs.
Separate facts from executable commands.
Log and diff intermediate artifacts.
requires-engineering: add schema validation between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are docs-only open-source tools with no stated residency, certification, or retention commitments. That means no specific compliance mismatch is evidenced, but also no documented controls are available to prove alignment. Because the rubric requires a concrete mismatch, this remains low and is driven by missing policy detail rather than a known violation.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through either agent, the absence of documented residency and retention controls becomes relevant.
IF the deployment requires HIPAA, GDPR, or FedRAMP guarantees, the current profiles do not evidence them.
mitigations: Confirm data-class handling before deployment.
Avoid regulated data until controls are documented.
Record retention settings for both agents.
requires-engineering: obtain vendor compliance attestations.
